literal: Morning having budded, day all mature bud having become, evening blooms this disease.
translation: This disease of love buds in the morning, swells into a mature bud all through the day, and blossoms fully in the evening.
modern: இந்தக் காதல் நோயானது காலையில் அரும்பாகி, பகல் முழுவதும் முதிர்ந்த மொட்டாகி, மாலையில் முழுமையாக மலர்கிறது.
explanation: The poet uses a beautiful botanical metaphor to describe the progression of lovesickness throughout the day. The pain of separation is compared to a flower that begins as a tiny bud in the morning ('arumpi'). As the day passes, it swells into a mature bud ('pōtu'), and when evening arrives, it fully blossoms ('malarum') into intense suffering. This illustrates how the loneliness of evening makes the pangs of love feel most acute.
